53500-the-romance-of-the-ranchos.title: The Romance Of The Ranchos
53500-the-romance-of-the-ranchos.creator: Unknown
53500-the-romance-of-the-ranchos.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In Los Angeles County, Ranchos Santa Monica, San Fernando, Azusa, La Canada, Puente and Tujunga all gave their names to the towns founded within their borders. Santa Ana and La Habra in Orange County likewise took their names from their ranchos.

arxiv-1712-08119.title: Search for electroweak production of supersymmetric states in scenarios with compressed mass spectra at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1712-08119.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1712-08119.description: Abstract A search for electroweak production of supersymmetric particles in scenarios with compressed mass spectra in final states with two low-momentum leptons and missing transverse momentum is presented. This search uses proton–proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider in 2015–2016 , corresponding to 36.

arxiv-2104-06069.title: 1-bit LAMB: Communication Efficient Large-Scale Large-Batch Training with LAMB’s Convergence Speed
arxiv-2104-06069.creator: Conglong Li, Ammar Ahmad Awan, *Hanlin Tang, Samyam Rajbhandari, Yuxiong He
arxiv-2104-06069.description: Abstract To train large models (like BERT and GPT-3) on hundreds of GPUs, communication has become a major bottleneck, especially on commodity systems with limited-bandwidth TCP network. On one side large batch-size optimization such as LAMB algorithm was proposed to reduce the frequency of communication.

arxiv-2106-04443.title: Robust Generalization despite Distribution Shift via Minimum Discriminating Information
arxiv-2106-04443.creator: Tobias Sutter, Andreas Krause, Daniel Kuhn
arxiv-2106-04443.description: Abstract Training models that perform well under distribution shifts is a central challenge in machine learning. In this paper, we introduce a modeling framework where, in addition to training data, we have partial structural knowledge of the shifted test distribution.

arxiv-2111-03965.title: Tensor Deblurring and Denoising Using Total Variation Thanks: Submitted to the editors October xx, 2021.
arxiv-2111-03965.creator: Fatoumata Sanogo, Carmeliza Navasca, Stefan Kindermann
arxiv-2111-03965.description: Abstract We consider denoising and deblurring problems for tensors. While images can be discretized as matrices, the analogous procedure for color images or videos leads to a tensor formulation. We extend the classical ROF functional for variational denoising and deblurring to the tensor case by employing multi-dimensional total variation regularization.

arxiv-2312-03612.title: Physical Symbolic Optimization
arxiv-2312-03612.creator: Wassim Tenachi, Rodrigo Ibata, Foivos I. Diakogiannis
arxiv-2312-03612.description: Abstract We present a framework for constraining the automatic sequential generation of equations to obey the rules of dimensional analysis by construction. Combining this approach with reinforcement learning, we built Φ \Phi -SO, a Physical Symbolic Optimization method for recovering analytical functions from physical data leveraging units constraints.

arxiv-2508-13122.title: A Kac system interacting with two heat reservoirs
arxiv-2508-13122.creator: Federico Bonetto, Michael Loss and Matthew Powell
arxiv-2508-13122.description: Abstract We study a system formed by M M particles moving in 3 dimension and interacting with 2 heat reservoirs with N >> M N>>M particles each. The system and the reservoirs evolve and interact via random collision described by a Kac-type master equation.

arxiv-2509-08105.title: Merlin : Multi-Stage Curriculum Alignment for Multilingual Encoder and LLM Fusion
arxiv-2509-08105.creator: Kosei Uemura, David Guzmán, Quang Phuoc Nguyen, Jesujoba Oluwadara Alabi, En-shiun Annie Lee, David Ifeoluwa Adelani
arxiv-2509-08105.description: Abstract Large language models excel in English but still struggle with complex reasoning in many low-resource languages (LRLs). Existing encoder-plus-decoder methods, such as LangBridge and MindMerger, raise the accuracy for mid and high-resource languages, yet large performance gap remains for LRLs.

pmc-10595467.title: Towards SDG30: Fighting HCV with a screening program in Lombardy
pmc-10595467.creator: A Meloni, S Piccinelli, C Marrocu, A Odone, D Cereda
pmc-10595467.description: BackgroundThe third Sustainable Development Goal, specifically in target 3.3, identifies fighting HCV as a priority.It is estimated that in Italy more than 200.000 patients eligible for HCV treatment are not being treated and 20% are not aware of the infection.

pmc-11407422.title: Adaptations to cationic biocide exposure differentially influence virulence factors and pathogenicity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
pmc-11407422.creator: Germán G. Vargas-Cuebas, Christian A. Sanchez, Elise L. Bezold, Gabrielle M. Walker, Shehreen Siddiqui, Kevin P.C. Minbiole, William M. Wuest
pmc-11407422.description: Cationic biocides (CBs), which include quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs), are employed to mitigate the spread of infectious bacteria, but resistance to such surface disinfectants is rising. CB exposure can have profound phenotypic implications that extend beyond allowing microorganisms to persist on surfaces.

pmc-12495448.title: Concurrent Tuberculous Meningitis and Toxoplasma Encephalitis in an HIV-Positive Patient: An Exceptionally Rare Case
pmc-12495448.creator: Lizi Adishvili, Shorena Dvali
pmc-12495448.description: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection is strongly associated with an increased risk of opportunistic infections affecting the central nervous system (CNS). Among these, tuberculous meningitis (TBM) and Toxoplasma encephalitis (TE) represent two of the most frequent and severe infections seen in individuals with advanced immunosuppression.

pmc-12751733.title: Coronavesicle-engineered hydrogel sequential photothermal-immunometabolic therapy reprograms tissue microenvironment for diabetic-infected wounds healing
pmc-12751733.creator: Bodeng Wu, Shan Lin, Qi Xiu, Mingzhen Zhong, Yiyao Huang, Zhenxun Wang, Xiuhua Wu, Jiangang Mei, Shuhan Liu, Liping Liu, Bo Li, Weilun Pan, Lei Zheng
pmc-12751733.description: Persistent infection and dysregulated tissue microenvironment constitute the primary obstacles hindering the healing of infectious diabetic wounds. Herein, we developed an NIR-responsive hydrogel dressing incorporating polyphenol-engineered plant-derived nanovesicles (termed Coronavesicles) via an in-situ deposition strategy, designed to implement sequential photothermal-immunometabolic therapy for infectious diabetic wounds.

pmc-13272628.title: ETV4 Improves Cerebral Ischemia‐Reperfusion Injury by Restraining YBX1‐GPX4‐Ferroptosis Cascades
pmc-13272628.creator: Qian Xu, Faming Deng, Dan Yu
pmc-13272628.description: BackgroundCerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a critical pathological process following ischemic stroke, with ferroptosis being increasingly recognized as a key contributor to neuronal damage. However, the regulatory mechanisms, particularly the role of specific transcription factors like E26 transformation‐specific variant 4 (ETV4), remain poorly understood.

pmc-13384033.title: A Supramolecular Thermal Switch for Precision Pyroptosis via Host−Guest Recognition and Electrostatic Interactions
pmc-13384033.creator: Dan Wu, Jie Zhou, Yibin Cao, Kunmin Ping, Borui Zhao, Yanrong Yang, Chunyang Yu, Xinyang Yu, Shaolong Qi
pmc-13384033.description: Cytomembrane‐puncturing gasdermin (GSDM)‐mediated pyroptosis activates antitumor immunity through the release of immunogenic cellular contents and proinflammatory cytokines. However, programmable and precise pyroptosis remains challenging due to the rigidity, inefficiency, and systemic toxicity of conventional inducers. Herein, a supramolecular thermal switch is engineered to enable precision pyroptosis induction.

pmc-13635001.title: Exercise-induced protein lactylation: From molecular mechanisms to precision health applications
pmc-13635001.creator: Wei Chen, Yifan Meng, Qiulin Zhong, Rengfei Shi
pmc-13635001.description: SummaryExercise-induced lysine lactylation of proteins is an important metabolic regulatory mechanism. This review systematically assesses how different exercise modes impact lactate post-translational modifications in a tissue-specific manner that in turn helps orchestrate energetic metabolic homeostasis, boost neuroprotection, and optimize cardiovascular adaptations.
